author: alanconfluent
body:
### Description 
Reverts #8248 and fixes the issue it was addressing.  Namely, the issue is that closing the forwarded connection after it had already been completed resulted in errors.  I'm not sure if this was the result of Vertx connection pooling somehow affecting other requests reusing the same connections, but this appeared to be the case.

The fix only closes the forwarded connection if the request is not complete by the time the connection to the proxy node is done.

This also has a fix for JSON parsing errors seen after we're given buffers that are not complete.  This is exactly what `RecordParser` is for, so it's used.

### Testing done 
Unit tests and manual verification.

- [ ] Ensure docs are updated if necessary. (eg. if a user visible feature is being added or changed).
- [ ] Ensure relevant issues are linked (description should include text like "Fixes #<issue number>")

   ### 6.0.2
   ```
   ----------------------------

- Namespace packages being measured weren't properly handled by the new code
  that ignores third-party packages. If the namespace package was installed, it
  was ignored as a third-party package.  That problem (`issue 1231`_) is now
  fixed.

- Packages named as "source packages" (with ``source``, or ``source_pkgs``, or
  pytest-cov's ``--cov``) might have been only partially measured.  Their
  top-level statements could be marked as unexecuted, because they were
  imported by coverage.py before measurement began (`issue 1232`_).  This is
  now fixed, but the package will be imported twice, once by coverage.py, then
  again by your test suite.  This could cause problems if importing the package
  has side effects.

- The :meth:`.CoverageData.contexts_by_lineno` method was documented to return
  a dict, but was returning a defaultdict.  Now it returns a plain dict.  It
  also no longer returns negative numbered keys.
   ```

This module works by using various built-in methods provided by OpenCV, including a model trained to detect faces. I will add explanations as I understand how it works myself.

This module also includes testing capabilities for a single image; just run the script in the command line with an argument specifying the path to an image with a face in it. (Example: `python face_recognition.py path\to\image.png`)

Next step will be to hook it up to video input to better test its capabilities, then look into how we could go about detecting the distance from the face to the camera. author: ignacio-chiazzo
body:
Fixed a bug in action_dispatch where routes with newlines weren't detected when using wildcard segments

### Summary

Original issue posted: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/39103

`Problem:` URL generation does not escape a newline character in a wildcard segment.

### Steps to reproduce it

```ruby
  draw do
    get "/wildcard/*wildcard_segment", to: SimpleApp.new("foo#index"), as: :wildcard
    get "/dynamic/:dynamic_segment", to: SimpleApp.new("foo#index"), as: :dynamic
  end

  assert_equal "/dynamic/a%0Anewline", url_helpers.dynamic_path(dynamic_segment: "a\nnewline") # succeeds
  assert_equal "/wildcard/a%0Anewline", url_helpers.wildcard_path(wildcard_segment: "a\nnewline") # fails with the error:
  # ActionController::UrlGenerationError (No route matches {:action=>"index", :controller=>"test", :wildcard_segment=>"a\nnewline"}, possible unmatched constraints: [:wildcard_segment]):
```

<details> <summary> Code snippet with tests passing </summary>

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails", github: 'ignacio-chiazzo/rails', branch: 'wildcard-routes'
end

require "rack/test"
require "action_controller/railtie"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.root = __dir__
  config.hosts << "example.org"
  config.session_store :cookie_store, key: "cookie_store_key"
  secrets.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  Rails.logger  = config.logger

  routes.draw do
    get "/" => "test#index"
    get "/dynamic/:dynamic_segment" => "test#index", as: :dynamic
    get "/wildcard/*wildcard_segment" => "test#index", as: :wildcard
  end
end

class TestController < ActionController::Base
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def index
    urls =
      dynamic_path(dynamic_segment: params[:s]) + "\n" +
      wildcard_path(wildcard_segment: params[:s]) + "\n"
    render plain: urls
  end
end

require "minitest/autorun"

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  include Rack::Test::Methods

  def test_generates_url_with_spaces
    get "/?s=a%20space"
    assert last_response.ok?
    assert_equal <<~BODY, last_response.body
      /dynamic/a%20space
      /wildcard/a%20space
    BODY
  end

  def test_generates_url_with_newlines
    get "/?s=a%0Anewline"
    puts last_response
    assert last_response.ok?
    assert_equal <<~BODY, last_response.body
      /dynamic/a%0Anewline
      /wildcard/a%0Anewline
    BODY
  end

  private
    def app
      Rails.application
    end
end
```

</details>

Note: See the original issue for more details.

### Code issue:

TL;DR The issue is that the Regex doesn't check for `multiline`. 

If there is a route that uses a wildcard (e.g.`/wildcard/*wildcard_segment`) and the client sends a URL like this`/wildcard/a%0newline`, the [`Formatter` class](https://github.com/ignacio-chiazzo/rails/blob/b5f2b550f69a99336482739000c58e4e04e033aa/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/journey/formatter.rb#L179) checks that the path `a\nnewline` matches against the REGEX `/\\A(?-mix:.+?)\\Z/`.

This REGEX uses the [Ruby opts:source](https://ruby-doc.org/core-2.2.0/Regexp.html#method-i-to_s) notation, but it's the same as `/\A#{/.+?/}\Z/`. Note that the regex embedded (`/.+?/`) doesn't use multiline (that's why we see `-mix`), which means that `multiline` (`m`), `extended mode` (`x`), and case sensitive (`i`) are disabled. 

To fix the issue I enabled multiline in the sub Regex when `wildcard` only. It looks like `wildcard` was disabled [on purpose](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/routing/mapper.rb#L256), I tried using git blame to see the reason behind but I couldn't find it (it's added a long time ago > 12 years)  [(latest commit I found)](https://github.com/ignacio-chiazzo/rails/commit/ca3936dbd691538d97d8dbe2bc1d64c21dc7db0e)

**Why does dynamic route work?**  dynamic paths don't have a `requirement`, so it doesn't check against a REGEX, [it just checks](https://github.com/ignacio-chiazzo/rails/blob/b5f2b550f69a99336482739000c58e4e04e033aa/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/journey/formatter.rb#L173-L176) that the value `dynamic_segment` is not nil.

### Reviewers

- Is there any security issue I'm ignoring here?
- Is there any reason not to allow `multiline` when using `wildcard segments` that I am missing?

author: mark-dce
body:
All tests in the GraduationJob test group are periodically failing
with the same error:
```
ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound:
  Couldn't find Hyrax::PermissionTemplate
./lib/workflow_setup.rb:156:in `block in everyone_can_deposit_everywhere'
./lib/workflow_setup.rb:154:in `everyone_can_deposit_everywhere'
./lib/workflow_setup.rb:44:in `setup'
./spec/jobs/graduation_job_with_embargo_spec.rb:46:in `block (3 levels) in <top (required)>'
```
See an example at https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/curationexperts/laevigata/504/workflows/bd115b16-c926-461a-b739-cb9c864d3763/jobs/536/tests#failed-test-0

This failure is occuring in the workflow setup called in the `before` block
for the test group.  It appears that depending on the randomized order of other
tests, the AdminSets and Workflow may be left in a state incompatible with
the workflow setup for this test group, causing the setup to silently fail.

Explicitly resetting Fedora to a clean state allows the workflow setup
to run successfully and leave Workflows in the state expected by
the rest of the test group.

author: uranusjr
body:
See #15072, cc @ephraimbuddy 

It turns out Connexion performs argument introspection to decide what arguments to pass to an endpoint (a bit like pytest fixtures), so we can't actually make the functions _too_ generic. For example, we must have a parameter named `connection_id` in various Connection endpoints, but that's obvious specific to Connection and cannot be refactored out. So this two-layer approach is the best I can come up with for now.

I'm not actually convinced myself if this is a good idea (it feels like a ton of architecture that makes code more difficult to understand), but at least now we have something to think about.

Schedules are now able to recognise clashes in events, and will not add events if they clash.

Some example of clashes are:

12/01/2021 from 1400 to 1600 and 12/01/2021 from 1400 to 1600 -> clash
12/01/2021 from 1400 to 1600 and 12/01/2021 from 1500 to 1600 -> clash

12/01/2021 from 1400 to 1600 and 13/01/2021 from 1400 to 1600 -> no clash
12/01/2021 from 1400 to 1600 and 12/01/2021 from 1600 to 1700 -> no clash

body:
In this PR, a simple beam background parser is implemented and the tool is used to load the data and rotate the position and momemtum. 

The python option could be configured as following:
```python
from Configurables import GtBeamBackgroundTool

beambackground = GtBeamBackgroundTool("GtBeamBackgroundTool")
beambackground.InputFileMap = {"default": "ToCEPCSW.out"}
beambackground.InputBeamEnergyMap = {"default": 120.} # GeV
beambackground.RotationAlongYMap = {"default": 16.5e-3} # radian
```

Presently, this causes a crash which is against the method contract (that should return an `empty()` instead).

author: bosvensson1
body: We currently use a version guard to adapt to a change in the number of parameters supplied to `osg::TriangleFunctor`'s `operator()` template functor. The differing parameter is unused in our code. Crucially, `operator()` is not an override, so we can just add a default value for the differing parameter. body:
If a task with the same hash exists in the destination, it is deleted first.

A conflicting integration task in the target is deleted first and the delete notifications are sent out, then the original task is moved.
In order to avoid having duplicated functionality the `teamId` was removed from `updateTask` mutation, so `changeTaskTeam` is the only way left to move a task.

## Testing
### Moving task between teams replacing existing task
#### Setup
* [x] create 2 teams Team A and Team B
* [x] join both teams with users Alice and Bob
* [x] Alice sets up Jira integration for Team A and Team B
* [x] Bob sets up Jira integration for Team B only
* [x] Alice starts a Sprint Poker in Team A and adds 4 tasks in the Scope stage via Jira integration (JIRA-1 - JIRA-4)
* [x] Bob does the same in Team B with the same 4 Jira tasks
* [x] Alice goes to their Tasks, Archived and un-archive the Jira tasks and distributes them in all 4 columns
* [x] Bob goes to their Tasks, Archived and un-archives JIRA-1 - JIRA-3 and leaves them in the default column
* [x] Open the sessions for Alice and Bob in separate browsers
#### Verification
* [x] Bob opens team B dashboard
* [x] Alice opens Tasks and changes the team of JIRA-1 task from Team A to Team B
* [x] While Alice is doing this, Bob observes the old Team B JIRA-1 disappearing and the new Team A JIRA-1 appearing
* [x] Repeat for JIRA-2 till JIRA-4, the tasks must appear in the right column for Bob
* [x] The archived JIRA-4 of Bob is gone

### Moving task to new team without integration
#### Setup
* [x] Clarissa creates 2 teams: Team Integration and Team No-Integration
* [x] Clarissa adds GitHub and Jira integrations to Team Integration
* [x] Clarissa creates a new GitHub and a new Jira Task

  * [x] a dialog is presented asking Clarissa to setup GitHub integration
* [x] Clarissa declines

* [x] Clarissa repeats the process but now presses 'Add it now'

  * [x] when successfull task is moved to Team Integration

author: dacamposol
body:
### Improve Dockerfile

- Added the RedHat base image that contains way less vulnerabilities than the official one

| [Official](https://snyk.io/advisor/docker/python) | [RedHat](https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/ubi8/python-38/5dde9cacbed8bd164a0af24a?container-tabs=security&tag=1-71&push_date=1632226439000) |
| ------- | -------- | 
| 13H 30M 133L | 8H 0M 0L |

- Get advantage of the layered cache: it doesn't make sense to install the requirements each time that the code is modified. The requirements should be cached as a layer and only rebuild it when the requirements file is modified. This will improve a lot the times between consequent Docker builds, since from second build and onward only the three last layers need to be rebuilt (bulding time of 1.1s on average with 10 tries) if just code is changed.
- Use the `.env.docker` file by default in the image if an `.env` file is not present in the repository. I saw there was a problem in #43 due to the lack of `.env` file meanwhile building and running the Docker image. This should fix the problem even if I agree a better README.md should be in place.

### Fix #51 

There's a known bug on APScheduler 3.6.3 due to it's dependency on tzlocal 3.0b1: agronholm/apscheduler#461

Solved with APScheduler 3.7.0 with no further changelog than bugfixing (already checked)

https://github.com/agronholm/apscheduler/compare/v3.6.3...v3.7.0

**Is this a patch, a minor version change, or a major version change**
I would say that this could be considered a minor version change, but it's at the decision of the maintainers.

author: rupl
body:
# HID-2283

We have users reporting errors when their email addresses contain capital letters anywhere in the address. This is because we store email addresses in DB all lowercase, and we weren't lowercasing them when doing password reset lookups.

Additionally, I noticed that emails aren't actually getting verified when password resets are successful, which can effectively lock someone out of their account permanently if they only have a primary email and never click the initial confirmation link. I got myself into this situation while testing locally with a fresh account.

While looking at this I removed the old `/new_password` routes which will only be used by emails that are a month old by the time we deploy to prod. I also renamed the template to `new-password.html` so that the whole directory is consistent with uses of dashes instead of underscores.

# Testing

1. Register new account with at least one CAPITAL letter in the email address `CAPITALS@example.com`
2. **Ignore the confirmation email**
3. Initiate a password reset by typing your new email with at least one capital letter. Note: it does NOT need to match what you typed when you registered. This is basically the bug we're fixing. e.g. `CaPiTaLs@example.com`
4. You should NOT see an error, and SHOULD see a message saying "if [email] exists, we sent a password reset link"
5. After resetting password, you should be able to login with your new password (despite having ignored the initial email confirmation link).

author: mdumandag
body:
This test failed in one of the maintenance runs against the 4.2.z branch, but not
much is changed in that part of the codebase, so, it must also apply to
master as well.

The test logs do not contain any suspicious lines for this test, it fails after
10 seconds, when the assertion timeout is passed, and the lock is still locked
despite the 2 seconds lease time.

I have gone over the implementation, but I couldn't find any buggy behavior
that would lead to such a failure.

That lead me to think that the test failed due to timing issues, and somehow
the thread that should schedule the expiration of lock couldn't be scheduled
in the assertion timeout seconds. I have verified that, if I delay the
expiration task, the test fails with the exact same logs. Moreover, the
diagnostics logs in the failed run show that the system was under heavy
load, so that might lead to such problems.

Closes #18742

body:
The changelog will be used as release notes for humans, and changelist will be used as metrics for systems (e.g. fourkeys). We have separated the render options because we want different output for each.

Example:
```
jobs:
  gh-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v1
      - id: release
        name: Execute gh-release
        uses: na-ga/actions-gh-release@separate-changelog-and-changelist-render-options
        with:
          release_file: 'RELEASE'
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          max_commits_number: 200
          changelog_only_use_merge_commit: true
          changelog_ignore_merge_commit: false
          changelist_only_use_merge_commit: false
          changelist_ignore_merge_commit: true
```

author: saifaqqad
body:
The commits do the following
* 0bdef4d: Fixes the window dragging issue on windows 11 by using `ACCENT_ENABLE_GRADIENT` instead of `ACCENT_ENABLE_BLURBEHIND`. it currently checks the minor version number in `A_OSVersion` to distinguish between windows 10 and 11.
* 3e03c30: Adds the method `SetWindowFillColor(colorHex)` which changes the accent policy to `ACCENT_ENABLE_GRADIENT` and sets the fill color to the passed `colorHex` which is a hex-formatted 6-digit RGB color. Using this method will make the UI look much better when the fill color is set to the same color as the background/titlebar.

  for example: 
  ```ahk
  neutron := new NeutronWindow()
  neutron.Load("Bootstrap.html")
  neutron.SetWindowFillColor("#343a40")
  ```
  https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47293197/137118968-a39df74a-47bd-4b50-b6e5-0abff80fa731.mp4

* c5d3c46: Adds an optional title parameter to the `Show()` method.
* The other commits only fix some typos I made in the comments and restore the file encoding to `UTF-8 with BOM` which for some reason was missing in the first commits I made.

There are sometimes multitouch events detected, when only a single touch should be detected under certain conditions. This lead to touch events on previous touch positions. The referenced bug is closed with "won't fix" with the justification it would be platform specific. But this is not correct. author: cvicentiu
body:
- [x] *The Jira issue number for this PR is: MDEV-17964*

## Description
This happens upon CREATE USER and DROP ROLE.

The underlying problem is that our HASH implementation shuffles elements
around when performing an update or delete. This means that when doing a
scan through the HASH table by index, in search of elements to delete or
update one must restart the scan to make sure nothing is missed if at least
one delete / update happened.

The handle_grant_struct code assumed that it is safe to continue by only
reexamining the currently modified / deleted element index, but that is
not true.

Missing to delete an element in the hash triggered the assertion in
the test case. DROP ROLE would not clear all necessary role->role or
role->user mappings.

To fix the problem we ensure that the scan is restarted, only if an
element was deleted / updated, similar to how bubble-sort keeps sorting
until it finds no more elements to swap.

author: janosh
body:
Follow up to #2247.

@CompRhys informed me that due to #2247, Pymatgen is no longer installable in Google Colab which is locked to Python 3.7 while `typing.Literal` was only added in Python 3.8.

There's a relatively recent but quiet issue tracking the ability to select different Python versions in Colab: https://github.com/googlecolab/colabtools/issues/2165

In the meantime though, I assume Pymatgen wants to keep supporting Google Colab. I think the best solution for that would be to protect `Literal` imports with

```py
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from typing import Literal
```

and then use the string form `"Literal"` in type hints. Happy to add those changes to this PR if that's acceptable.

Fixes #[issue_no]

## Summary of Changes
<!-- Please provide a summary of changes for this pull request, ensuring all changes are explained. -->
Flap / Slat movement will use a simple model that will only allow movement if there is hydraulic pressure.

The model takes a flap/slat surface position command from SFCC1 and SFCC2 computers. An unresponsive SFCC will cause its corresponding hydraulic motor to stop.

Note that only one duplicated SFCC is simulated in this PR, actual dual SFCC implementation will follow in a separate dedicated PR.


Flaps/Slats speed is converted into hydraulic motor speeds using the actual 1:314.98 actuator arm to torque shaft ratio.

It reports an angle in Feedback Position Pickup Unit (FPPU) degrees.

This is a simple model but yet will handle partial pressure from two circuits, and should have correct flow consumptions.
Transients in flow and motors RPM are just simplified low pass filters.

Normal operation should be as before. Check the motion of flaps and slats has no glitch when it's moving.

When only blue pressure is available, only slats will deploy in around 35s.

When only yellow epump + ptu is present, full slat/flap deployment should be extremely slow (more than a minute).

When only GREEN and YELLOW engine pumps are active and blue epump disabled, Flaps should move close to full speed, slats should move at half speed.

When only GREEN engine pump is active and blue epump disabled, Flaps should move at half speed, slats should move at half speed.

When only YELLOW engine pump is active and blue epump disabled, Flaps should move at half speed, slats should not move.

## Description
 * Recently a change was introduced to modify the default value of s3 plugin's permanent URL toggle from NO to YES. author: otacke
body:
If the `Column.isTask` function does not report a content type to be a task (usually scorable), but the content type sends out xAPI statements, then Interactive Book may decrease the number of tasks left by 1 and this leads to a wrong count of interactions on the summary screen.

This can, for instance, happen for Agamotto that is not considered to be a task (not scored), but sends out xAPI `completed` once all images have been shown.

When merged in, the number of tasks left will only be reduced by 1 if the instance at hand is considered to be a task.

author: vaf-hub
body:
I implemented this such that we check if the `exstingEvent` has different properties than the ones we keep track of in the `CalendarEventViewModel`. There are two issues with this approach, though:

1. The organizer does not have a way to force sending updates to every attendee, unless they make a change (such as changing the description). See 2 for why we might really need this.
2. If an attendee sends a response to the invitation to the organizer, the event is in a different state than what was initially sent to other attendees and we might want to distribute the attendee status to everyone because other attendees might need to know who is attending and who not. Since the responses by the attendees are automatically processed, they are already included in the `existingEvent` when createing the `CalendarEventViewModel` and thus the user is not asked whether they want to send updates, even though some attendees do not know about each other's status.

The easiest solution would probably be a button to force sending updates to everyone, (before this was possible by just opening the `CalendarEventEditDialog` and clicking "Save".)

closes #3492

author: antalszava
body:
**Context**

At the moment, in the latest workflows we are pinning to the master branch explicitly using the `@master` suffix when specifying the URL for PennyLane.

`pip` can, however, produce dependency conflicts when a plugin pins PennyLane without the `@master` suffix. This is the case now for the [PennyLane-SF plugin](https://github.com/PennyLaneAI/plugin-test-matrix/runs/3883242440?check_suite_focus=true#step:5:55).

**Changes**

Removes the `@master` suffix when requesting PennyLane in the latest plugin workflows.

This ensures that several components in our ecosystem work well together, provided we pin to the `master` branch of PennyLane  using the `git+git://github.com/PennyLaneAI/pennylane` syntax:
* Plugins (e.g., [PennyLane-SF atm](https://github.com/PennyLaneAI/pennylane-sf/blob/d5188553bdb19ee758a0464cfdc08e19505bcd06/requirements.txt#L2));
* QML repo ([`dev` branch requirements](https://github.com/PennyLaneAI/qml/blob/dev/requirements.txt#L14));
* `plugin-test-matrix` (with this PR).

author: shayne
body:
Hey bud., great project!

A couple changes in this pull request...

Typically you don't include the `node_modules/` folder in your repo. These dependencies make code reviewing a lot harder  and makes repo operations slower because you're including TONS of files in your repo, none of which you're maintaining.

Since we're removing 'node_modules/`, it means we'll have to "get them" when we clone to the project to work on it. This is typical, and achieved by running `yarn` or `npm i` (depending on which package manager you're using).


The other change I made was removed the `.env` file. I saw that you didn't have your secret in there, good job on that! `.env` files are typically not included in the repository. What you might find and could include is a documented `.env.example` to give other developers a leg up when getting started.

Also, `.env` is typically used for development purposes and in production you'd set the environment variables on the container running the bot. Happy to help you with that.


So we removed `node_modules/` and `.env`, how do we keep them from coming back? Well that's where the `.gitignore` file comes in handy. It tells git to ignore these files/folders and not include them as part of source control. The .gitignore I included seems a little overwhelming but it's really just a boilerplate standard ignore file for Node projects. I just Googled "gitignore node" and it was the first result. 

I did add ".env" to the top of the ignore file since that is more specific to our project. Upon second look it was already included in the boilerplate Node ignore file since it's a common file/pattern for Node projects.

body:
## Motivation

This abstracts the configuration detailed in https://interlok.adaptris.net/blog/2017/09/04/interlok-proxy.html as code.

In situations like Heroku, which only allows you to expose a single external port. If you have an API endpoint serviced by Interlok but also have jolokia enabled then you're a little bit screwed.

## Modification

- Completely new optional management component
- Does not actually have a dependency on interlok-rest-base 
- Should 100% test coverage (via mocks + an embedded undertow instance).  

## PR Checklist

- [x] been self-reviewed.
- [x] Added javadocs for most classes and all non-trivial methods
- [x] Checked that new 3rd party dependencies are appropriately licensed
- [x] Added comments explaining the "why" and the intent of the code wherever it would not be obvious for an unfamiliar reader
- [x] Added unit tests or modified existing tests to cover new code paths
- [x] Checked that javadoc generation doesn't report errors

## Result

- New management component that can be configured; tested against jolokia but could be useful in other situations where you have that style of workflow in place. 
- Since it is a management component, you can protect the endpoint via use a security-constraint (or similar) + **jaspi.** in the same way that you might project the health-check endpoints.

## Testing

- Build a project that depends on interlok-jolokia + `org.apache.httpcomponents.client5:httpclient5:5.1`
    - you probably want to have one called 'MyInterlokInstance' so you can cut and paste the commands below.
- Build this management component and copy it in place

- bootstrap.properties (such that we auto-proxy http://localhost:8080/jolokia -> http://localhost:8081/jolokia)
```
managementComponents=jmx:jetty:jolokia:proxy
interlok.proxy.1=/jolokia::http://localhost:8081
```
- Then you can follow the instructions from https://interlok.adaptris.net/interlok-docs/#/pages/advanced/advanced-jolokia?id=jolokia-monitoring-and-management-400 

```
$ curl --location -si --request POST 'http://localhost:8080/jolokia/' --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --header 'Accept: application/json' --data-raw '{
  "type" : "READ",
  "mbean" : "com.adaptris:type=Adapter,id=MyInterlokInstance",
  "attribute": "ComponentState"
}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: no-cache
Server: Jetty(9.4.43.v20210629)
Pragma: no-cache
Expires: Wed, 13 Oct 2021 12:23:07 GMT
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2021 13:23:07 GMT
Content-Type: application/json;charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

{"request":{"mbean":"com.adaptris:id=MyInterlokInstance,type=Adapter","attribute":"ComponentState","type":"read"},"value":"StartedState","timestamp":1634131387,"status":200}
```
- You can compare and constrast the output if you hit `http://localhost:8081/jolokia` (which is where the jolokia management component is listening

## Bonus testing because that's how we roll.

- Build this configuratrion as docker image and start it, but only expose 8080 (`-p8080:8080`) and attempt to connect to it via the UI running elsewhere.

- significant speed optimizations by querying all tables and columns in a schema in one shot, rather than on a per-table basis. in my case, querying ~175 tables, it's about **40x faster**. added `$schema` option to config file so people can query the correct schema, but if that's not set i filter default system schemas so most users don't even need to set this.
- a nice bonus of this is i'm able to get the primary key from mysql at the same time, so i deprecated the `$primaryKey` option entirely (particularly nice for legacy databases like mine where i previously had to use a lambda to query each table's primary key because they're all weird). this much better addresses issue #48. not a breaking change.
- added a script execution timer

author: adamnovak
body:
Dependabot is now regailing us with PRs. I've tried to wrap a bunch of suggested version bumps into one PR, so we can actually test and merge them in reasonable time, and widened some of our version specifiers so we don't need to intervene every time a new dependency patch release happens.

I also made some tweaks to setup.py to avoid duplicating the cwltool version.

## Changelog Entry

author: avin1100
body: ## Motivation Currently, shuffle accounts makes a key for the user from the new_account.key checked into the repo. Now shuffle accounts will generate a new random private key for the user. If the user already has a previous key (from using shuffle account in the past), then they will be prompted if they want to actually switch their key. If the user says "y", a new key and address will be generated and saved in their primary key location (/accounts/latest). The old key and address will be saved in a folder containing the timestamp via duration since epoch of system clock. ## Test Plan I ran cargo run -p shuffle -- account from my terminal. I looked in my .shuffle/accounts directory and see that there is this /latest folder holding my latest key/address pair: When I ran cargo run -p shuffle -- account again, I was prompted if I wanted to switch keys. I answered y, and a new private/public key pair was generated and a new address was claimed. I looked in my /accounts directory and noticed a folder with timestamp 1634142234 show up. This folder has the previous key and address. When I ran cargo run -p shuffle -- console, I noticed my address was shown. Note that shuffle console only uses the most up-to-date key found in the accounts/latest folder: ## Related PRs (If this PR adds or changes functionality, please take some time to update the docs at https://github.com/diem/diem/tree/main/developers.diem.com, and link to your PR here.)

author: nwalters512
body: I noticed that some questions that contained many course issues contained a very unhelpful instructor message: After digging into this a bit, I realized that we were actually caching the results of operations that included course issues. Since course issues are represented as Error objects, that explains the meaningless error message: we can't round-trip Error objects through Redis, so when we retrieve them, they're just JSON objects, and calling `.toString()` on them to get the instructor message would result in `[object Object]`. This PR updates the freeform question code to avoid writing data to the cache if it contains a non-empty `courseIssues` array. It also updates the code for retrieving data from the cache to silently ignore anything from the cache that contains a non-empty `courseIssues` array. This can be removed once this has been deployed to production for a while. See the inline comments for more details.

author: raphblanchet
body:
## 📖 Description
🧠 New feature : Integration of a `RepeatablePublisher` that will reexecute a block after the specified duration, until cancelled. This is useful for publishers that need to be repeated indefinitely to refresh the returned value. 

A utility function `repeat` has been added to `Publishers` to ease the creation of such publisher. 

It is also possible to add `.repeat(x)` to an existing publisher to make it repeatable

## 💭 Motivation and Context
Some use cases need the publisher to be refreshed every specified duration, which was not "easily" possible without this feature.

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?
This code comes from 2 other projects that integrated their own `RepeatablePublisher`, so now we bring it to `trikot.streams`. Some unit tests have also been added!

## 🦀 Dispatch
- `#dispatch/kmp`

body: ## Description **Issues:** - closes #668 **Background:** Many users may want to favourite/bookmark/pin or "save" posts that they really liked or simply want to come back to later. This is possible to achieve once a user has interacted with a post, but it could certainly be made more convenient by creating the ability to "save" posts - which seems like a nice convenience we can give to our Premium members to add further value there. This PR builds a new Premium feature that allows users to save/bookmark/pin posts and access their list via a new filter action in the _My Feed_ page's advanced filters. Originally, I was going to add it to the My Posts page, but it would actually require quite a lot of tricky refactoring of our `TabToggle` component and that entire mechanism, and I also realised it fits better in the My Feed page anyway, since by definition these aren't "your posts". **Implementation:** - I implemented the core functionality with a little "bookmark" icon, since a lot of people are used to this from places like Instagram which uses a more or less identical icon, combined with the "save post" terminology. - Also implemented Optimistic UI directly via the cache for both optimal User Experience and performance/saving DB requests. - For accessing the list, a user can use a new _filter action_ called "saved posts" within _Advanced Filters_ on the My Feed page. - Since I'm not sure about the final wording we want to go with, on a DB level I used the generic term "save" (`savedPosts`) so that it will still make sense even if we change the user-facing terminology later - I chose to add this as a simple field on the `User` and let Prisma manage the relationship, as we do with `followedUsers`, rather than creating a new table. ## Subtasks - [x] I have added this PR to the Journaly Kanban project ✅ - [x] Database changes & migration - [x] Resolvers - [x] GraphQL - [x] Build out Post Page UI & wire everything up for saving/unsaving posts - [x] Build out UI for My Feed Page - [x] Wire up `posts` resolver to take new `savedPosts` arg - [x] Implement toast messages for saving/unsaving - [x] Implement Premium Feature Modal / guard on _Post_ & _My Posts_ pages - [x] Translations - [x] Add to Feature Comparison Table 🌟 ### Deployment Checklist - [ ] 🚨 Publish new j-db-client version and update in both `web` and `j-mail` - [ ] 🚨 Deploy migs to stage - [ ] 🚨 Deploy code to stage - [ ] 🚨 DEPLOY `j-mail` to stage - [ ] 🚨 Deploy migs to prod - [ ] 🚨 Deploy code to prod - [ ] 🚨 DEPLOY `j-mail` TO PROD ## Migrations - Does the migration need to be applied before or after deploying code? - **Before** - Is applying the migration going to necessitate downtime? - **Negativo** - Is there any SQL or backfill logic that has to be run manually? - **Nein** - Are the DB changes high risk in your estimation? Should a manual DB snapshot be taken before applying? - **Low risk** ## Screenshots **1. Post - Unsaved State** **2. Post - Saved State** **3. My Feed - New Filter Action**

author: bobvanderlinden
body:
###### Motivation for this change

Docker has quite a few configuration options. You can see them here: https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/dockerd/#daemon-configuration-file

Some of these can be set using command-line options and thus using `virtualisation.docker.extraOptions`, but some of them are only available using the JSON configuration file. One example is `log-opts`.

In addition, serializing `types.anything` to JSON results in a nicer way to configure docker. For comparison:

```
extraOptions = "--ipv6 --fixed-cidr-v6 fd00::/80";
```
with:
```
daemon.settings = {
  ipv6 = true;
  "fixed-cidr-v6" = "fd00::/80";
};
```

This also allows the use of the mk* functions in order to modularize the configuration better.

Do note that anyone who has created `/etc/docker/daemon.conf` in the past to configure Docker ad-hoc must now migrate this configuration to NixOS's configuration. I have added a incompatibility note in the release notes.

###### Things done

I cherry-picked this commit to an older revision that I was able to build. I ran the docker tests:

```
nix-build nixos/tests/docker.nix
```

I confgured my system using:
```
  virtualisation.docker = {
    enable = true;
    daemon.settings = {
      ipv6 = true;
      "fixed-cidr-v6" = "fd00::/80";
    };
  };
```

I switched my system:

```
nix flake update --override-input nixpkgs $HOME/projects/nixpkgs && sudo nixos-rebuild --flake . switch
```

After that, the systemd service looks as follows:

```
$ systemctl is-active docker
active
$ systemctl cat docker
...
ExecStart=/nix/store/5m6801fx87daw9cd63dkii7qv998647s-docker-20.10.9/bin/dockerd \
  --config-file=/nix/store/pi1kc96nflwhaxzzfx295ds93j2fsh2p-daemon.json \
  

```

The config file looks as follows:

```
$ cat /nix/store/pi1kc96nflwhaxzzfx295ds93j2fsh2p-daemon.json                                                       
{
  "fixed-cidr-v6": "fd00::/80",
  "group": "docker",
  "hosts": [
    "fd://"
  ],
  "ipv6": true,
  "live-restore": true,
  "log-driver": "journald"
}
```

author: makfill
body:
**1. Task:** https://github.com/rolling-scopes-school/tasks/blob/master/tasks/react/pointing-poker.md
**2. Deploy:** https://pointing-poker-be--dev.herokuapp.com
**3. Technologies used:**
- Express
- Socket.io
- TypeScript
- PostgresSQL
- Sequelize
- Axios
- logger: Winston and Morgan
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/75532397/137190850-53492250-4c96-44bc-b224-88300e264368.png)

**4. Description:**

The backend exchanges information with the front by means of http requests, at the start of the application, and by means of a web socket for users in one room.
All information about the state of the rooms is stored in the database. Postgre is used as the database, Sequelize is used as the ORM for working with the database.
In the database, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships are used between tables, which made it easy to implement multi-rooms and the ability for one user to be an admin in one room, and a user in another room. Also, these links will make it easy to scale the application if necessary.
The main tables are Room, StateRoom, RoleUser, User, Task, Messange.
The Room table is linked to the Messange, Task, StateRoom tables by a one-to-many relationship. A many-to-many relationship with the User table.
The User table is linked to the Messange table in a one-to-many relationship. With RoleUser, Task tables, many-to-many relationships.

body:
While developing a [bare-bone gemini client library](https://github.com/omar-polo/gemini) for clojure, I took a look at this implementation for things like accepting self-signed certs.  One thing that I noticed is that java doesn't seem to send SNI (server name indication) by default (FWIW I'm running `jdk-11.0.12.7.1v0`.)

The gemini specification requires SNI, and various servers will refuse to accept requests from clients that doesn't provide one.

This PR adds SNI to requests, I've tested locally against [gmid](https://gmid.omarpolo.com/) and seems to work.  I have still some problems to browse the geminispace using jgemini thought.

(I'm using the same code in [Request.java](https://github.com/omar-polo/gemini/blob/main/src/com/omarpolo/gemini/Request.java#L114) for my little library.)

author: justingrant
body:
We recently made progress in adding more typing to the [temporal-polyfill](https://github.com/js-temporal/temporal-polyfill) TS implementation, and doing this exposed quite a few bugs in our old types. Also, it made sense to add some new types for options and units.

This PR rolls up recent changes from the prod polyfill:
* Options properties are now all marked as optional
* Different implementation of singular vs. plural unit-name string literal types
* Prevent `RoundOptions<'bogus'>`
* New exported unit-name literal types: `DateUnit`, `TimeUnit`, `DateTimeUnit`
* `PluralUnit<T>` type to convert singular to plural.
* new types: `LargestUnitOption<T>`, `SmallestUnitOption<T>`, `TotalUnitOption<T>`
* Narrowed parameter types of `Calendar` and CalendarProtocol methods, e.g. requiring either `month` or `monthCode`, or requiring `year` or `era`/`eraYear`.
* Added missing `toJSON()` on `Calendar` and `CalendarProtocol`.  It's required on the former, optional on the latter.
* Fixed `Calendar.from` to return a `CalendarProtocol`, not `Calendar`.
* Added `era` and `eraYear` to *Like types. (They were already on class types.)
* Removed `PlainTime` as an argument to PlainTime's `add` and `subtract`. This was probalby an old copy/paste bug.
* Fixed `TimeZone.from` to accept a `TimeZoneProtocol`
* Fixed `timeZone` property of `ZonedDateTime` to be `TimeZoneProtocol`
* Renamed exported Intl namespace to be `Intl`, not `IntlPolyfill`. When our types previously extended `Intl`, they'll extend `globalThis.Intl` now.
* Added a `DateTimeFormatOptions` type as an interim measure until TS lib types catch up. Corrected the options type of `DateTimeFormat` to use this new type.

author: jbum
body:
The issue:

Twice in the past two weeks, CovidStateDashboardTable, a complex Cron job that produces several sets of tables, has reached the 10-minute mark (likely during the Github tree-building portion, which is slow). When this happens, the Cron gets unceremoniously killed by Azure, and needs to be rerun manually. Typically, the Tests and/or Hospitals jsons are generated, but we lose Cases/Deaths, which are processed last.

This patch addresses this issue in several ways:

1. It splits the Cron into three separate Crons (Cases/Deaths, Hospitalizations, Tests) so that the overall run-time per Cron is shorter.

2. It no longer schedules the Crons on the hour, but instead staggers them 7:05, 7:10, 7:15. There is some anecdotal reporting on the Internets that Github is particularly slow on the hour, due to the prevalence of jobs that fire on the hour.

3. The SQL jobs have been split into two -- one for cases/deaths/tests (a single query is currently used for all these), and one for the hospitalization data, which is retrieved separately. This causes a minor reduction in SQL querying and validating time. The content of the SQL queries has not been modified (which is why cases/deaths/tests are still combined).

The new Crons have been tested locally, and the Cases/Deaths one was used this morning to resupply those files.

To link a pull request to an issue to show that a fix is in progress and to automatically close the issue when someone merges the pull request, type the keyword "Closes" followed by a reference to the issue. For example, Closes #404 or Closes Virtual-Coffee/virtualcoffee.io/issues/404.

## Description

<!--

A pull request description describes what constitutes the Pull Request and what changes you have made to the code.

It explains what you've done, including any code changes, configuration changes, migrations included, new APIs introduced, changes made to old APIs, any new workers/crons introduced in the system, copy changes, and so on. You get the gist.

@mention individuals that you want to review the PR, and mention why. (“ @username I want to know what you think of this code.”)

-->
This PR re-enables eleventy-plugin-pwa, and attempts to avoid pre-caching of pages that are "thank you" pages users arrive at after submitting a form.

## Methodology

I used the `globIgnores` option for eleventy-plugin-pwa and the underlying workbox. For now the best I could figure is to target the pages that have "thank" in the path, corresponding to these templates:
`src/forms/report-coc-violation/thanks.njk`
`src/forms/lunch-and-learn-submissions-thanks.njk`
`src/membership-thankyou.njk`

If it would be better to find ways of avoiding caching more explicitly let me know.

As for testing, I ran `yarn start` locally and verified that the files weren't listed in Application Cache under Chrome Developer Tools, where they were before I fixed the globIgnores pattern.

author: mpenick
body:
This approach fixes prepared cache validation by registering an
`EventListener` to invalidate external prepared cache whenever relevant
schema change event occur. This means that the cache can no longer be
asynchronous and will possibly suffer from a prepare stampede when the
same query is run many times simultaneously.

The drawback of this approach is the very rough invalidation of the
cache and complexity. The invalidation of the cache can be quite broad
i.e. if we're unable to determine the keyspace and/or table of a
prepared statement we have to invalidate it because we don't have enough
metadata to see if it's still valid or not.

author: toxiapo
body:
This PR updates the atEnd function to use `clientHeight` instead of `scrollHeight` for calculating the remaining page content.

The bug appears when loading a reflowed page on scroll mode on firefox. On scroll mode, some margin and padding were added through CSS to the  <body> tag inside the Iframe document, making the Iframe to overflow, clientHeight returns the actual viewable height of the document, which is what we want.

## To Reproduce

- run `npm run example:react` with this book. https://drb-files-qa.s3.amazonaws.com/epubs/gutenberg/65303_noimages/manifest.json
- Switch to scroll mode, the next page button does not take you to the next resource.

author: pau-tomas
body: * **What kind of change does this PR introduce?** (Bug fix, feature, docs update, ...) Feature * **What is the current behavior?** (You can also link to an open issue here) Custom Script only allow for Variables to be used as arguments when being called. * **What is the new behavior (if this is a feature change)?** When calling a custom Scripts that has Variable arguments, the fields for those now allow to select `number` or `variable` as an option. * **Does this PR introduce a breaking change?** (What changes might users need to make in their application due to this PR?) No. The case where the argument is a variable and not an union (which will happen in old instances of the custom script events) is still covered in the `callScript` method (kind of forced by typescript as the actor parameters still come as a string in that case). * **Other information**: I wonder if we should rename the `Variable A...J` parameters inside the custom script to `Number A...J`? As it might become a bit confusing?

<!-- If there's already an issue that this PR fixes, add that issue number below after 'Fixes #' -->
Fixes #729 

## Description of the Change

The `client_secret` is effectively not a secret if stored as plaintext. This becomes a security risk if a database is compromised, especially for 2-legged OAuth2 (client credentials flow) where there is no other mitigating credential to be used in authentication.

NOTE that this preserves the existing behavior of *not* hashing `client_secret` by default. To enable it, it must be explicitly set. In theory this should provide backwards compatibility with existing installations.

### Description
Adds a basic e2e test for `firebase deploy --only extensions`. This test deploys 2 extensions, then verifies that they were successfully installed via `firebase ext:list --json`.

I also made some changes to listExtensions, so that the output of `firebase ext:list --json` would be simpler to parse. Once this command is ready to merge publicly, I'll add this test to our CI as well.

`npm run test:extensions-deploy`

author: emely3h
body:
Test Aufbau
Der Test ist aufgeteilt in zwei verschiedene Usergruppen (= Threadgruppen): Gäste und alle Anderen (Studenten + Dozenten + Hochschulmitarbeiter). Diese führen jeweils checkins auf 2 verschiedene Räume durch (test room + A007a => muss auf Testserver angepasst werden) durch und einige GET-Anfragen auf die Startseite und das FAQ. Die Daten für die Usergruppen beim Checkin werden durch ein phython script erstellt. Die resultierende csv Datei und das script ist ebenfalls beigefügt. Die genaue Anzahl der Anfragen ist im jeweiligen Ordner der Thread Gruppe definiert. Dabei können 3 verschiedene Parameter variiert werden:

Number of Threads: Anzahl an User
Ramp-up period: Zeit zwischen dem starten des nächsten Threads
Loop Count: gibt an, wie oft der komplette Prozess wiederholt werden soll => bei 2x werden alle einmal ein und wieder ausgecheckt

Doku zum jmeter maven plugin: https://github.com/jmeter-maven-plugin/jmeter-maven-plugin
Anleitung zum Starten der Tests mit maven: https://it-qa.com/how-does-maven-integrate-with-jmeter/
Um die Ergebnisse 'schön' in einem Graphen anzeigen zu lassen kann ein weiters plugin integriert werden: https://github.com/codecentric/jmeter-graph-maven-plugin

author: laimiux
body:
## What
Introducing a new `Snapshot<Input, State>` type to be used in `evaluate`
```kotlin
interface Snapshot<out Input, State> {
    val input: Input
    val state: State
    val context: FormulaContext<State>
}
```

This will allow us to change `evaluate` from 
```kotlin
fun evaluate(input: Input, state: state, context: FormulaContext<State>): Evaluation<Output>
```
to a simplified by slightly more implicit signature of
```kotlin
fun Snapshot<Input, State>.evaluate(): Evaluation<Output>
```

Also, this change should make it easier to add `Input` to `FormulaContext` which will allow us to automatically pass `Input` parameter to transitions (similarly to how the state is currently passed).

body:
### Team
@FrozenKiwi

### Use case
A stablecoin your granny could (and should) use - familiar banking interface, no hashes to be seen.  The user shouldn't know that the underlying tech is crypto.

author: vuqtran88
body:
## Description

A customer experienced a deadlock in their app on startup. This is because the customer is using a configuration builder which made external request using HttpWebRequest on startup. This call triggered the agent to start but agent couldn’t start because it tried to read app settings which depends on the configuration builder. This caused the external call to hang then the app. The fix is to add "System.Net.HttpWebRequest.GetResponse" to the DeferInitializationOnTheseMethods list to delay this external call instrumentation after the agent successfully starts.

This PR also removes confusing/incorrect logging message.
